title: Modified Rankin Scale (mRS)
sources: van Swieten JC, Koudstaal PJ, Visser MC, et al. Interobserver agreement for the assessment of handicap in stroke patients. Stroke. 1988;19(5):604-607 (modified scale).
Rankin J. Cerebral vascular accidents in patients over the age of 60. Scott Med J. 1957;2(5):200-215 (original scale).

changelog.change: Initial entry — a genuine content gap. The near-universal stroke functional-outcome measure, used as the baseline/premorbid reference point alongside NIHSS and ASPECTS in thrombectomy decision-making, and as the standard outcome measure in every major stroke trial.

purpose: The standard measure of functional independence after stroke — used both as a baseline (premorbid mRS) input to thrombectomy eligibility and as the outcome measure in essentially every stroke trial.

tiers.description: No significant disability despite symptoms — able to carry out all usual duties and activities.
Slight disability — unable to carry out all previous activities, but able to look after own affairs without assistance.
Moderate disability — requires some help, but able to walk without assistance.
Moderately severe disability — unable to walk or attend to own bodily needs without assistance.
Severe disability — bedridden, incontinent, requires constant nursing care and attention.

interpretation.label: A baseline (premorbid) mRS is part of thrombectomy eligibility screening
interpretation.detail: Most major thrombectomy trials required a premorbid mRS 0-1 for enrollment — a patient already at mRS 3-4 at baseline changes the risk/benefit conversation, not the acute NIHSS/ASPECTS alone. mRS 0-2 at 90 days is the standard 'good outcome' threshold reported in stroke trials.

buildNote: classification engine, matching the killip-classification / postpartum-hemorrhage-staging pattern. Pairs with nihss and aspects (both already built) in the stroke-decision workflow — cross-referenced via aliases/keywords since calculators don't carry a `related` field.
